title: Bias vs Variance
analogy: Werewolf archers aiming silver arrows at glowing jack-o'-lantern targets in the midnight fog. High bias: Arrows all clump into the same wrong spooky dead oak. High variance: Howling wildly, arrows scatter all over the dark cemetery. The master archer stays close and consistent.
concept: Bias is error from overly simple assumptions (underfitting). Variance is error from sensitivity to training data (overfitting). Making a model more complex lowers bias but raises variance, so you look for the sweet spot.

quiz.q: A very simple model that misses the pattern has...
quiz.why: Consistently wrong: all silver arrows stuck in the wrong spooky oak tree.
More flexible means fitting training pumpkins better but wobbling wildly on new data.
